ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Jane Austen

code.originalText: Six-week review: electrolytes, renin, blood count, and recovery

text.paragraph: Six-week review: electrolytes, renin, blood count, and recovery. [S]

Ms. Austen returns six weeks after starting replacement and ten days after the streptococcal sore throat, during which she doubled her hydrocortisone for three days and then went back to her usual dose; she finished the amoxicillin yesterday. The illness settled without vomiting or any emergency. Her energy now lasts until early evening, and she writes for most of the morning. The salt craving and the lightheadedness have gone, and she has had no back ache for over a week. She thinks the darkness of her hands is fading. She wears her medical ID. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-30; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: 114/72 lying, pulse 72; 112/72 after three minutes standing, pulse 78: no postural drop
Pigmentation of the hands and face lighter; gum patches unchanged; no signs of glucocorticoid excess
The tender neck nodes from the sore throat have gone; no cervical, supraclavicular, axillary or inguinal nodes

About three months of increasing tiredness, loss of 5 kg, darkening of the skin, nausea with bouts of vomiting, low back ache, salt craving and lightheadedness on standing, with low sodium, high potassium and raised eosinophils; adrenal insufficiency suspected and urgent endocrinology testing booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation; its timing echoes the documented break in her health (D).

Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease): no cortisol response to cosyntropin with a markedly raised ACTH, and mineralocorticoid deficiency with raised renin and low aldosterone; on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone; synthetic modern diagnosis chosen for a historical illness whose cause is disputed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the historical cause of her illness remains undetermined (R, disputed).
Mild normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL) with normal ferritin, vitamin B12 and folate
S — Synthetic finding at intake; it recovers on replacement.
Group A streptococcal pharyngitis with fever, treated with amoxicillin and doubled hydrocortisone under the sick-day rules; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.
